question: If a triangle has a perimeter of 52 units, then all its sides have length ________ units.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the triangle inequality theorem, any side of a triangle must be strictly less than half of its perimeter.

Maximum possible length of a single side [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the triangle = 52 units.

**Formula Used:**

According to the triangle inequality theorem, the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side.

 

 a

 c
 Perimeter = a + b + c = 52
 Triangle Inequality: a + b > c

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sides of the triangle be a, b, and c.

⇒ The perimeter is the sum of all sides: a + b + c = 52

⇒ From the triangle inequality theorem: a + b > c

⇒ Add 'c' to both sides of the inequality:

⇒ a + b + c > c + c

⇒ Substitute the perimeter value (a + b + c = 52):

⇒ 52 > 2c

⇒ Divide by 2:

⇒ 26 > c, which means c [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Triangle Inequality Theorem (Difference)

The difference between the lengths of any two sides of a triangle is always strictly less than the length of the third side (|a − b| < c).

Perimeter & Semi-perimeter

The perimeter is the total boundary length (P = a + b + c). The semi-perimeter (s) is half of the perimeter (s = P ÷ 2), heavily used in Heron's formula for the area: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)].

Types of Triangles Based on Sides

Scalene (all three sides are of different lengths), Isosceles (exactly two sides are equal), and Equilateral (all three sides are equal, each measuring exactly one-third of the perimeter).
